summary: This RFC reproduces a letter from a Department of Defense official transmitting the National Research Council report on transport protocols and requesting specific actions on its recommendations. It was replaced by RFC 1039.

plainLanguage.summary: This RFC reproduces a Defense Department letter about a report on transport protocols. The letter asks an agency to prepare for testing and possible use of the protocol recommended in the report.

questions: what did the dod say about the nrc report
what did the dod say about transport protocols
what did the report recommend for dod networks
subtitle: A Defense Department letter about recommendations on transport protocols.

tldr.problem: The National Research Council recommended a course for the Defense Department on transport protocols for its data networks.
tldr.mechanism: The reproduced letter sends the report to the Defense Communications Agency and asks it to prepare requirements, participate in standards work, enable testing, and plan a possible transition.
tldr.outcome: RFC 945 is listed as obsoleted by RFC 1039.

today: RFC 945 was obsoleted by RFC 1039, according to the unit metadata.

sections.title: Why the Report Was Requested
sections.content: The RFC explains that earlier Defense Department memoranda required TCP/IP for packet networks with potential host-to-host connections across network boundaries. It also describes a policy of using suitable non-Defense standards when available. Questions about TCP/IP and international standards led the Defense Department and the National Bureau of Standards to ask the National Research Council to study the issue.
sections.plainLanguage: The Defense Department had required TCP/IP, while also considering international standards. It asked the National Research Council to study the choices.

sections.title: The Report's Recommendation
sections.content: The letter transmits the National Research Council's report on transport protocols for Defense Department data networks. The letter says the report recommends adopting the ISO Transport Protocol TP-4 and Internetwork Protocol IP as co-standards alongside the existing TCP and IP standard, then moving ultimately toward exclusive use of TP-4. It also states that TP was not then available as a proven commercial offering.
sections.plainLanguage: The report recommended testing TP-4 alongside TCP/IP, with possible later movement to TP-4. The letter says TP was not yet a proven commercial offering.

sections.title: Actions Requested from the Agency
sections.content: The Assistant Secretary asks the Defense Communications Agency to develop military requirements for TP, provide representation to commercial standards working groups, prepare its protocol test facility for TP testing, and develop a transition strategy with resource estimates. The letter also asks the agency to evaluate detailed recommendations in the report as they apply to that strategy.
sections.plainLanguage: The agency is asked to write down requirements, take part in standards discussions, prepare to test TP, and plan what a transition would require.
